issues.situation: The way it picks a target conflicts with the measured positions. At s7453 (Custodes mirror, P2, round 1) the measured gain (+6.17, n36) is a creep toward obj_center that keeps all of Guard Beta on home. In the planner obj_center is a lost race. My replication of the race arithmetic gives 16 enemy OC vs max(9, 14) at the Advance pace and 25 vs 24 walking; the narrow designer's log also shows race_lost=true. _keeper_reach_check skips lost races, so that move is never tried. Even if it were, obj_nml_1 (27.2) is tried first, best score first, and is accepted with OC 3. The designer's own 6-seed check of the nml_1 creep gave E(hold - fix) = +0.67 [-3.96, 5.30]: no gain. At s7454 the measured move (+4.83) leaves home; the keeper had 1 model on the area, so no creep can reproduce it. At s7433 it fires toward an unmeasured target (obj_nml_2). So 0 of 2 findings move, and both of its round-1 fires go to flank objectives that nothing measured. Underlying problem: the creep is valued with the capture score of a trip the keeper never continues. Next turn the same rule cannot move it further without leaving the area, holders never re-centre, and KEEPER-RELEASE is home-only and never fired in the bench.
issues.proposed_change: Do not ship. If the idea is revived: allow lost-race targets for a creep (it does not commit the keeper to the race). Choose among the creeps by where they end (for example closest to obj_center or the most contested objective, since both measured gains were centre moves), not by capture score. Then re-measure that exact move at s7453 and s7433 before any bench run.

issues.situation: It cannot fire in round 1 of any bench fixture, so the bench cannot show its effect. I computed this from mirror_custodes_2000_postdeploy and asym_2000_postdeploy. U_CUSTODIAN_GUARD_F (5 models, M6, OC 2 each) stands on the near edge of area-large-14, with its centroid 5.0" from the marker on the centre side. A full 6" move toward obj_center or obj_nml_2 keeps 0 of 5 models on home, and _find_safer_position keeps the full move (threat 0.00 -> 0.05). The only move that keeps OC is toward obj_nml_1 (2 of 5, OC 4), and that target is a lost race (31 vs 10 in the mirror, 32 vs 10 in asym), which the check skips. P2 is the mirror image and only worse after P1 moves. In mirror_orks_2000_postdeploy and on the asym Ork side, 4-5 units stand on each home at the start, and KEEPER-REACH needs a sole keeper. Any bench difference can therefore only come from round-2+ creeps that nothing measured. The fix that matches the evidence (a centre creep) is geometrically impossible from this deployment.
issues.proposed_change: Do not spend bench games on it. Any revival must first show [KEEPER_REACH] fires over a few seeds in each of the three bench fixtures. Expect identical pairs otherwise, as V9's KEEPER-RELEASE gave (64/64).

issues.situation: need = max(enemy_oc, projected_enemy_oc) + 1, which is 1 on any held_safe objective. So the design accepts creeps that cut the keeper's OC on the objective, and the cut is permanent: a 'hold' order always returns REMAIN_STATIONARY, so the keeper is never re-centred. At s7453 home_2 goes from OC 6 (2 models in range) to OC 3 (1 model) for rounds 2-5. With OC 3, which is at or below ENEMY_WEAK_OC_FLOOR (4), the opponent's planner rates our home as enemy_weak (+7) instead of enemy_strong (-5). P1's Allarus, IN_RESERVES at that decision, can Deep Strike from round 2 onto the far side of the 11.5" x 7" ruin, more than 9" from the lone model, and out-OC it (6 > 3 instead of a 6-6 tie). That flip lands at P2's round-3 Command phase, after the one-round rollout horizon. If an enemy later comes within 12", the smaller friendly OC also raises home's reinforcement need, pulling another unit back. The need also ignores Advance, reach to the hosting area (up to ~6.7" beyond the marker on these areas) and reserves; KEEPER-RELEASE counts all three. In the bench the realistic fire is an Ork back-edge keeper: Warbikers D creeping 12" toward the centre keeps 2 of 6 bikes (OC 6 -> 4).
issues.proposed_change: Only creep when the OC kept in range is at least the keeper's current in-range OC (no OC lost). Size the next-turn threat with _keeper_release_threat's reach model (Move + Advance to the hosting area, plus reserves that can arrive), not the marker-based projected_enemy_oc.

issues.situation: The trigger is broader than the evidence. There is no is_home check, no round limit and no score margin: KEEPER-RELEASE requires +5, this needs only score > hold. Every measured sole-keeper position is round 1, and almost all are home; none is a held_safe sole holder in rounds 2-5. The design fires for NML and centre sole holders in any round. In round 4 it can creep toward a 2-turn target it can never complete, because it must stay to keep the objective; the round 4-5 stay bonus (7) exists to stop exactly that. For Orks the home stay bonus is divided by aggression (1.8), so the score gate barely filters anything.
issues.proposed_change: Limit it to our home objective in battle rounds 1-2 and require KEEPER_RELEASE_MIN_GAIN over the hold score.

issues.situation: Plan order and merge with the round-3 revision (68c03f7). The creep is applied after pass 2 through apply_capture_assignment. (a) Pass 2.5's melee chase gate then treats the keeper as a mover: the chase cap is max(20", M+14") instead of the hold limits of 10-14", and unit_is_on_objective is measured against the target. If the gate converts it to ATTACK, only the target's need is re-opened (action != 'hold'), not home's, and the new dict drops keeper_reach_*, so the executor safety net never runs. A melee-seeker keeper (for example Thunderwolf Cavalry, the s7420 guardrail unit) then leaves home with no backfill. 68c03f7 guards exactly this case for KEEPER-RELEASE. It does not occur in the bench: Guard spears are S5 A2 ranged, and Ork bikes and koptas have strong guns. (b) The target's OC need, planned_new_objs and pass 3's support ledger now count a unit that will not arrive. (c) 68c03f7 deletes the hunk's context (V9's post-pass-2 release loop).
issues.proposed_change: Apply it after pass 3, next to the revised release, and only if the keeper's assignment is still 'hold' on that objective. Skip _is_melee_seeker keepers. Set the move fields directly instead of calling apply_capture_assignment, so nothing is consumed at the target.

issues.situation: Exposure. TerrainManager.is_model_hidden is per model, so models moved outside the dense ruin lose 13.09 Hidden and the unit becomes targetable beyond 15" (this matters against the Stompa and Ork guns in asym). _charge_leaves_held_objective calls _unit_oc_at_position and _get_oc_at_position without the hosting area, so it uses the 3.79" marker circle. A keeper at the ruin's edge (5+" from the marker) therefore gets no CH-LEAVE penalty and can be charged off home. The gap exists in the base too; the creep makes it worse by moving the keeper toward the enemy. Also, an Advance-priced long-trip candidate (RACE-1) is used unchanged for a Normal-move creep.
issues.proposed_change: Pass the hosting-area objective and mm to the OC helpers in _charge_leaves_held_objective (an independent fix). Count lost Hidden in the creep's cost, and re-price with _keeper_release_normal_pace from 68c03f7.

reviews.fires_in_bench: Round 1: 0 in all three fixtures. I computed this from the fixture saves; I did not run Godot. Custodes mirror and Custodes vs Orks: the home keeper U_CUSTODIAN_GUARD_F (and F_P2) stands on the near edge of its 7" x 11.5" home ruin. Toward obj_center or obj_nml_2 a full 6" move keeps 0 of 5 models on home, and the threat model doesn't shorten it. The one move that keeps OC (toward obj_nml_1, 2/5) is a lost race (31 vs 10 mirror, 32 vs 10 asym), which the check skips. P2 is the mirror image. Orks: 4-5 units stand on each home at the start, and KEEPER-REACH needs a sole keeper. Rounds 2-5: rare. The Custodes home keeper can only creep toward the flank NML objective, which stays a lost race while the enemy is there. Ork sole home keepers (M12) can keep OC from the back or side of the ruin: Warbikers D 2/6 and Deffkoptas B 4/6 in the Orks mirror, asym Warbikers A 3/3 toward the centre. The Ork home stay bonus is divided by aggression, so there will be occasional round 2-3 fires on the Ork side, and occasionally an NML or centre sole holder. My estimate is about 0-0.5 fires per game overall. Most pairs will be identical, as V9's keeper fix gave (64/64). Any differences will come from round-2+ creeps that nothing measured. No bench unit starts in reserves, and the check draws no RNG, so a non-firing check cannot desynchronise paired games.
reviews.strengths:
The diagnosis is right: on 11e terrain objectives, 'leaving would drop control' is sometimes false, and s7453's measured move did stay on home. The build is careful:
- It predicts the move with the executor's own _compute_movement_toward_target and checks range with MissionManager.model_in_objective_range.
- The executor re-checks the actual destinations and stands still on a mismatch.
- It respects fragile keepers, HOLD_OBJECTIVE earmarks and the DIM-RETURNS/FAR-TRIP vetoes.
- It leaves KEEPER-RELEASE's threat model, and its round-3 test, untouched.
- It is gated by a param, with a test that restores base behaviour.
- It draws no RNG.

The report is candid: it says its s7453 move measured no gain and that s7454 is not fixed.
reviews.summary:
Drop. As written, KEEPER-REACH does not make the measured move at either finding.

- **s7453:** the +6.17 target, obj_center, is a lost race in the planner (16 vs 14 at the Advance pace, 25 vs 24 walking), so _keeper_reach_check never tries it. It creeps toward obj_nml_1 instead. The designer's own 6 seeds show no gain for that move (+0.67 for holding), and home OC drops from 6 to 3.
- **s7454:** the measured +4.83 move leaves home, which a creep can't reproduce.

Its valuation is unsound on both sides:
- **Gain:** it is priced as the capture score of a trip the keeper never continues. The next creep would leave the area, holders never re-centre, and KEEPER-RELEASE never fires in the bench.
- **Cost:** need = enemy OC + 1, which is 1 on a safe objective. So it accepts creeps that permanently cut home's OC, and nothing in a one-round rollout sees the later Deep Strike or fast-unit flips or the weaker enemy view of our home.

It also fires on any objective in any round with no score margin. Its order relative to pass 2.5 lets a melee-seeker keeper be turned into a hunt with no backfill; the round-3 revision (68c03f7) already guards this for KEEPER-RELEASE and also removes this patch's hunk context.

Most decisive for shipping: from the fixture saves, it cannot fire in round 1 of any bench game. The Custodes keeper stands on home's near edge, so moves toward the centre or obj_nml_2 keep 0 of 5 models and the only OC-keeping target is a lost race; the Ork homes start with 4-5 units. Later fires are rare (about 0-0.5 per game, I estimate), so the bench would show mostly identical pairs. A narrower version (no OC lost, lost races allowed, home only, rounds 1-2) would probably pick s7453's centre move, but it still could not fire in the bench, so it cannot be shipped through the bench either.

Patch and report: /home/user/warhammer-40k-godot/tools/ai_lab/r4_designs/keeper_reach/root.patch and root.json. My replication scripts are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-warhammer-40k-godot/72451711-ff9e-5f4b-a27c-d739a3534701/scratchpad/ (reach_geom.py, race_sim.py, threat_sim.py).

issues.situation:
The KEEPER-REACH post-pass runs after pass 2 and BEFORE pass 2.5 (COORD-4 attack-intent conversion). It rewrites the keeper's assignment as a `move` to the target. Pass 2.5 then judges the keeper with the mover rules of `_melee_chase_gate`:
- There is no hold distance limit. For Custodes (aggression 1.5) a holding keeper chases only within 18" in R1, 14" in R2 and 12" in R3+. A moving keeper chases anything within the 20" cap (max(20, M+14)), measured centroid to centroid.
- `unit_is_on_objective` is measured against the target, so the contested and late-game protections never apply.

In the bench fixture saves, Custodian Guard ARE melee seekers (ranged Guardian spear S4 A2 is not 'strong'; melee S7 AP-2 D2). A concrete case: Custodes mirror, round 1, P2's turn.
1. P1's Guard C advances toward the centre and ends about 19.7" from Guard F P2 (centroid 1115,1739).
2. KEEPER-REACH fires: Guard F P2 creeps toward obj_nml_2 and keeps 2/5 models on home.
3. Pass 2.5 converts Guard F P2 to ATTACK. The base AI would hold, since 19.7" > 18".
4. Because the action is `move`, pass 2.5 re-opens only the target's `oc_consumed`, not home's need (the `hold` branch's h_threat - h_left + 1).
5. The rebuilt attack dict drops keeper_reach_*, so the executor safety net never runs. The keeper advances off home and no unit backfills it.

Even within 18", home's need is no longer re-opened. Running the post-pass before pass 2.5, backfill and pass 3 also changes other units' bookkeeping (target OC consumed, `planned_new_objs`) away from the measured plan. Round-3 revision 68c03f7 hit exactly this problem for KEEPER-RELEASE and guards it.
issues.proposed_change:
Move the KEEPER-REACH post-pass after pass 3, next to 68c03f7's KEEPER-RELEASE post-pass, and copy 68c03f7's guards:
- Apply it only while `assignments[uid]` is still `hold` on `kh.objective_id`.
- Skip it, logging "[KEEPER_REACH] ... stands still — moving, it would go hunting X", when `_melee_chase_gate(unit, uid, kh_t (action move), enemies, friendly_units, snapshot, player)` is non-empty.

Add a unit test: a melee-seeker keeper whose creep keeps OC, with an enemy 19" away in round 1, still holds, with the same plan as FIX_KEEPER_REACH=0.

issues.situation:
In `_select_movement_action`, the ROLLOUT override does `assignment = assignment.duplicate()` and replaces only action, objective_id, objective_pos, distance and reason. keeper_reach_home, keeper_reach_pos and keeper_reach_need therefore survive.

A forced Normal move to another objective (the usual critic alternative, e.g. "move U_CUSTODIAN_GUARD_B_P2 to obj_center") then reaches the new executor check against home. If the forced move leaves home's range, the executor returns REMAIN_STATIONARY, and the override (already marked used) is silently replaced by a hold.

Any future value check of a position where KEEPER-REACH fired, with a 'move elsewhere' alternative, would measure hold vs creep under the alternative's label. This only affects counterfactual rollouts, not games.
issues.proposed_change: In the ROLLOUT block, erase "keeper_reach_home", "keeper_reach_pos" and "keeper_reach_need" from the duplicated assignment. Alternatively, run the executor check only while `assignment.objective_id` is still the planned target. Add a test where an override with these keys present is executed as forced.

issues.situation:
`_keeper_reach_check` takes the first trip that keeps OC, in planner-score order.

At s7453 that is obj_nml_1 (score 27.2; 28.5" away; keeps 1 of 3 models = OC 3). The centre creep (score 20.8, the move measured at +6.17) keeps all 3 models (OC 9). My straight-line check and the report's branch-B end position (1040,1705) agree on this. The designer's own 6-seed check of the obj_nml_1 creep gave E(fix - hold) = -0.67 [-5.30, 3.96]. s7454 does not fire. So the design fixes 0 of 2 findings in a measured way.

In the bench Custodes fixture, the only trips that keep OC are toward the side objectives (P1 Guard F to obj_nml_1, P2 Guard F P2 to obj_nml_2). That is the unmeasured variant.
issues.proposed_change:
Rank the trips that keep OC by OC kept in range first, then by score. That picks the centre at s7453 and obj_nml_2 at s7433.

Optionally, require oc_in >= the OC the keeper has in range now (no OC loss). This also covers the next issue, but would likely stop the round-1 bench firing (Guard F: OC 10 to 4).

Before benching, measure the fix's actual choice, not the critic's alternative, at s7453, s7433 and the round-1 bench keeper positions.

issues.situation:
need = max(enemy_oc, projected_enemy_oc) + 1, and projected_enemy_oc counts only enemies within M+2". It ignores Advance, charges and reserves, which is the gap that sank REINFORCE-CAP.

In the bench, the round-1 creep leaves 2 of 5 Guard models on home (OC 10 to 4). In later rounds the hold branch keeps the unit where it stands (REMAIN_STATIONARY), so home stays at reduced OC against later threats.
issues.proposed_change: When `_keeper_release_threat` (worst-case reach plus reserves) reports a threat, require no OC loss. Alternatively, size `need` from that worst-case reach instead of projected_enemy_oc.

issues.situation:
The change is broader than the evidence and the report has gaps:
- KEEPER-REACH applies to the sole keeper of ANY objective (there is no is_home check), but all the evidence is about home keepers.
- Cluster guardrail s7452 (Prosecutors, sole holder of obj_nml_1) is missing from guardrail_checks. The fragile exclusion should keep it unchanged, but the report does not say so.
- The 'fires' estimate (about 0-1 per game) comes from finding positions, not the bench fixtures.
- root_cause says 6" for an M8 unit.
issues.proposed_change: Restrict to `ev.is_home`, as KEEPER-RELEASE does, or justify creeps on no-man's-land objectives. Add s7452 to the guardrail checks. Replay the round-1 positions of the three bench fixtures and count firings.

issues.situation:
Test quality. The test pins the override on and erases it, and drives the real planner (`_evaluate_all_objectives` + `_assign_units_to_objectives`). Its firing case fails on base for the right reason (4 asserts) and param 0 holds. Gaps:
- The new executor re-check and the emitted BEGIN_NORMAL_MOVE / REMAIN_STATIONARY are never exercised.
- Only the circle fallback is used. There are no source_pieces, so the 11e hosting-area path behind s7453 is untested.
- The late fragile exclusion has no test.
- test_keeper_holds_when_the_enemy_is_on_its_way puts the enemy 8" away. The objective is then held_threatened and the base branch decides, so the test passes on base and never reaches KEEPER-REACH's need logic.
- There are no chase-gate or ROLLOUT cases.
issues.proposed_change:
Add these cases:
- `_select_movement_action` with a planned keeper_reach assignment: a move that keeps home gives BEGIN_NORMAL_MOVE whose destinations keep >= need; a move that leaves gives REMAIN_STATIONARY.
- A terrain-hosted objective (source_pieces).
- A fragile keeper.
- An M12 enemy about 15" from a held_safe home (need > 1).
- The chase-gate and ROLLOUT cases from the two major issues.

issues.situation:
Style and merge points:
- keeper_reach_hold_oc is written and never read.
- An Advance-paced trip candidate is relabelled `move` without re-pricing turns_to_reach, so the FAR-TRIP veto judges the Advance pace. 68c03f7 re-prices the walk with `_keeper_release_normal_pace`.
- On top of 68c03f7, this block's anchor (V9's KEEPER-RELEASE post-pass after pass 2) no longer exists.
- A keeper whose release is vetoed after the pass never gets the KEEPER-REACH check, because `keeper_released.has(uid)` was already true in pass 1.
- Cost is fine: at most (objectives - 1) `_compute_movement_toward_target` probes per sole keeper, once per plan.
issues.proposed_change: Drop keeper_reach_hold_oc. Re-price the walk at Normal-move pace before the FAR-TRIP veto. After the merge, also evaluate KEEPER-REACH for keepers whose release was vetoed.

reviews.fires_in_bench:
Likely to fire, mostly in round 1 of the Custodes fixtures. This is unverified: neither the designer nor I replayed a bench fixture.

- **Custodes mirror:** each home starts with exactly one sole keeper (Guard F / Guard F P2, 5/5 models on the 7"x11.5" home ruin, near its enemy-facing edge). A straight 6" move toward the side objective in its own half keeps 2/5 models on the area (OC 4 >= need 1 in round 1): P1 toward obj_nml_1, P2 toward obj_nml_2. Every other trip, including the centre, keeps 0. It should fire whenever that side trip outscores holding and passes FAR-TRIP/DIM-RETURNS. Estimate: about 1-2 fires per game, so games diverge from V9 (unlike KEEPER-RELEASE's identical pairs). The moves are side-objective creeps that reduce home OC from 10 to 4, the variant with no measured gain, not the measured centre move.
- **Custodes vs Orks:** P1's Guard F behaves the same (about 1 per game); the Ork side about 0.
- **Orks mirror:** about 0. Three or four units start on each home, so there is no sole keeper in round 1. Later keepers have M12-14 or are fragile, so a full move almost never keeps a base on the area.

The pass-2.5 ATTACK conversion (major issue 1) can also occur in the Custodes mirror: P2, round 1, when a P1 unit ends 18-20" from Guard F P2.
reviews.strengths:
- **Diagnosis.** Accurate and matches the saves: s7453 is blocked by its card (Determined Acquisition counts home, exclude_home false); s7454 is blocked by KEEPER-RELEASE's worst-case reach (Immovable Object excludes home). The designer checked that the measured centre move at s7453 actually kept home.
- **Honest report.** s7453 is marked PARTIAL with a check showing no gain for the design's own move, s7454 is marked NOT FIXED, and a prototype that broke a must-pass KEEPER-RELEASE test was reverted.
- **Prediction.** Uses the same range test that scores objectives (MissionManager.model_in_objective_range on 11e hosting areas, with a conservative centre-distance fallback) and the executor's own `_compute_movement_toward_target`. The executor re-checks the blended destinations, so a mispredicted move falls back to standing still.
- **Gating.** Param 0 restores base exactly; every new path is gated. The probe uses no AI RNG and logs no errors, so a check that does not fire leaves games identical.
- **Logging and exclusions.** No debug logs are removed, and [KEEPER_REACH] lines appear at every decision point. KEEPER-RELEASE is untouched. Fragile and HOLD_OBJECTIVE keepers are excluded, and home's OC stays counted, so no unit is pulled onto home.
- **Cost.** Bounded: at most (objectives - 1) movement probes per sole keeper, once per plan.
- **Test.** Exercises the real planner, fails on base for the right reason and pins param 0.
reviews.summary:
Revise. The idea is sound under 11e rules: a sole keeper on a large terrain objective can move and keep control, and the s7453 branch-B result supports this toward the centre. Param gating and logging are clean, and the report is honest and matches the code and the saves.

Two real bugs:
1. **Melee-chase relabel.** The post-pass relabels the keeper `move` before pass 2.5. In the bench, Custodian Guard are melee seekers (ranged spear S4 A2), so the mover chase rules (20" cap, no hold limit) can send the keeper hunting. Home's OC need is then never re-opened, so home is dropped with no backfill. Round-3 revision 68c03f7 fixed exactly this for KEEPER-RELEASE: it releases after pass 3, requires the keeper still be `hold`, and re-checks the chase gate.
2. **Rollout override.** A ROLLOUT 'move' override keeps the keeper_reach_* keys and is silently turned into a hold, which would corrupt future value checks.

Separately, choosing trips by planner score picks obj_nml_1 at s7453 (OC 3, no measured gain) over the measured centre creep (OC 9), and s7454 is not fixed. So 0 of 2 findings are fixed in a measured way. In the bench it will likely fire in round 1 of the Custodes fixtures, but only as side-objective creeps that cut home OC from 10 to 4.

Recommended changes:
- Move the post-pass after pass 3 with 68c03f7's hold-still and chase-gate guards.
- Erase the keeper_reach_* keys on rollout overrides.
- Rank trips by OC kept (and consider a no-OC-loss rule).
- Add executor, terrain-area, fragile, chase and rollout tests.
- Measure the fix's actual moves before benching.

issues.situation: The backup is never made to retake home, so a release abandons it. On its own base (V9) the design still relies on V9's backup test after pass 2. That test counts any near-home unit that has no assignment yet, and pass 2.5, the COORD-4 backfill and pass 3 all run after it. The Custodes mirror (mirror_custodes_2000_postdeploy) is the only bench fixture where KEEPER-REACH fires: P1, round 1, Guard F/Zeta is the sole keeper. The nearest P2 model is 23.4" from the home area, inside V9's max-roll 24" but outside the new M+12 = 18". There the only backup still free after pass 2 is the Prosecutors. The V9 bench record /tmp/v9check/20261030_163105_CHK_M1_96021.record.json.gz shows pass 3 sending them to 'screen at (760,1446)', about 19" past the home area. Guard C advances to the centre and Guard D to nml_1. So every bench release leaves obj_home_1 with no unit within one move for rounds 2-5. The reserve backup is just as unenforced, and it is the mechanism behind s7453, the only finding the design changes. Deep-strike spots are rings at 10/12/15" around objectives plus a 4" grid. Each spot scores 10 minus distance near any objective that needs OC, plus 3 when it is 10-15" from an enemy. So the Allarus lands by a forward objective, not on our empty home. The 'home VP for one scoring' price then really covers every remaining scoring (Determined Acquisition: 3 VP x up to 4). Every cost after the end-of-round-2 rollout horizon is invisible to the +6.17.
issues.proposed_change: Make the backup real in the same phase. When a KEEPER-REACH release is applied, give the cheapest on-board backup (moves <= 1) its own candidate onto home, with assign_pass 'keeper_backup', so pass 2.5, the backfill and pass 3 skip it. If none can be pinned, keep the keeper. On 68c03f7 (release after pass 3): when the finished plan has no backup near home, reassign a backup whose job is screen or support to home instead of vetoing. Count a reserve unit only with a registered round-2 arrival on home: for example a static keeper_reserve_backup[player] that _decide_reserves_arrival reads to bring that unit in first and limit its landing objectives to home. Otherwise, when the card pays for home, price home at every remaining scoring, which keeps the keeper.

issues.situation: The release never reads the opponent's primary card. The new reach check unlocks 7 home-excluding P1 cards in the Custodes-mirror bench. In 3 of those 7 pairings the opponent's card pays for holding our home: Meatgrinder vs Meatgrinder (5 VP at the end of each enemy turn, rounds 2-5), Outmanoeuvre vs Outmanoeuvre (10 VP at the end of any enemy turn) and Delaying Action vs Punishment (8 VP at end of game). The opponent's planner adds enemy_home_bonus 7.5 or 15 toward our home. With V9, Guard F (OC 10) holds home all game and P2's race there is a lost race (halved). After the release, home is empty (issue 1) or held by a 45-pt fragile backup, so P2 commits units and scores 5-10 VP per turn from round 3. One-round rollouts cannot see this.
issues.proposed_change: In the KEEPER-REACH branch of _keeper_release_check, read mm.player_primary_missions[str(3 - player)]. Keep the keeper when that card has a hold_enemy_home rule scoring in rounds >= 2 (eot or command). For an end-of-game rule, add its VP to the required margin once.

issues.situation: Release and destination use different gates. The release is justified by `target`: score >= hold + KEEPER_RELEASE_MIN_GAIN + priced home VP + secondary VP, not a lost race. But the unit goes to `best`, which only needs score >= hold.score and may be a lost race. When the soonest objective is not the high-scoring one, the AI gives up home (and Determined Acquisition's 3 VP a scoring) for an objective worth about the same as holding. In the bench the centre is both soonest (2 Normal moves for Guard F) and usually top-scoring, so this seldom bites.
issues.proposed_change: Apply the same gate to `best` (score >= hold + min_gain + home_vp + sec_vp, not race_lost); otherwise keep `target`.

issues.situation: It does not merge cleanly with 68c03f7, the base it will be merged onto. The design sets target.action = 'move' inside _keeper_release_check and keeps the candidate's Advance-pace turns_to_reach, race_lost and score. 68c03f7 re-prices the walk with _keeper_release_normal_pace and refuses TOO-LATE or hopeless (RACE-SKIP) walks only when kr_t.action == 'advance', so a pre-converted 'move' skips both checks. The [KEEPER_REACH] 'released' report loop sits after V9's post-pass-2 block, which 68c03f7 deletes, so that line would never print. The early returns are {} where 68c03f7 returns {kept: why}, so the reason is lost.

issues.situation: The charge clause in _keeper_reach_threat compares model centres (mp.distance_to(nm[0]) <= (M+13)"). Charges are measured base to base, so two 40 mm bases add about 1.6", and more for Ork bikes or the Stompa. The near-home test uses base-edge distance, so the charge path is underestimated by the two base radii.

issues.situation: test_priced_home_primary_releases_a_big_gain asserts a release if the gain beats hold+5+3 and a hold otherwise, so it passes whatever the board produces. It cannot catch a pricing regression. No test covers the bench geometry (an M6 enemy 23.4" from a terrain home area, the backup sent to screen by pass 3). issues.proposed_change: Build boards with a known gain on each side of the threshold and assert one outcome each. Add a test that a released keeper's backup is within one move of home in the finished plan. Write a KEEPER-REACH-specific reason into coordination_note.

reviews.fires_in_bench:
On its own base (V9) it fires only in the Custodes mirror, only with the candidate as P1, only in round 1. That is about 1 in 4 of those games, about 1 in 8 Custodes-mirror games and about 4% of the whole bench. It never fires in the other two fixtures. Merged onto 68c03f7 as planned, it fires about 0 times, so the bench pairs come out identical.

Why it fires there on V9:
- The keeper (Guard F) is the sole unit on home. The nearest P2 model is 23.4" from the home area: inside V9's 24" max-roll reach (which is what blocked V9) but outside the new M+12 = 18". The charge clause does not trigger: P2 is more than 30" from our near-home units.
- P1 needs one of the 7 cards that exclude home: Immovable Object, Purge and Secure, Unstoppable Force, Meatgrinder, Reconnaissance Sweep, Delaying Action, Outmanoeuvre. That is 28% of seeds. The priced cards (Determined Acquisition +8, Secure Asset +9, Triangulation +15) rarely pass their margin.
- The V9 record shows the centre beating holding by 5.04 even under Punishment, so under home-excluding cards the margin should usually pass.
- The backup test after pass 2 passes, because the Prosecutors have no assignment yet at that point.

Why it does not fire elsewhere:
- P2 seat in the Custodes mirror: about 0. P1 has already moved, so P2's targets are lost races (V9 record: centre 27.57 includes contest_race -13.08) and P1's units sit within 18" of P2's home.
- Orks mirror: 0. Four units stand on each home, so there is no sole keeper.
- Custodes vs Orks: 0. Wazdakka (M14, about 24.3" away) and a Deffkilla Wartrike (M12, about 23.6") are inside M+12 of P1's home, and P2's Ork home is held by 5 units.

On 68c03f7, the backup test runs after pass 3 and needs a unit near home in the finished plan. In the V9 record none is: Guard C goes to the centre, Guard D to nml_1, and the Prosecutors screen about 19" past the area. The design's own trigger statement ('our reserves non-empty') understates firing on V9: on-board backups make reserves unnecessary, and the bench has no reserves.
reviews.strengths:
- The reach model is correct to the rules. A charge needs a target, so with nobody of ours near home an enemy can only walk onto it. M+12 covers a Normal move plus Advance, and also Speedwaaagh's flat 24" Turbo Boost for M12 bikes. Charge-then-consolidate through our near-home units is modelled.
- It correctly stays blocked in Custodes vs Orks.
- It keeps s7454's hold because of the enemy Deep Strike reserve.
- V9 releases are unchanged (s7437 kept). Every guardrail is untouched (s7451, s7420, s7455, s7458, s7433). Fragile keepers and plan HOLD earmarks still keep.
- It is limited to round 1, gated by FIX_KEEPER_REACH, and logged under [KEEPER_REACH].
- Cards it cannot price (hold_more, markers, require_hold_home) still veto.
- It sends a durable unit forward, the opposite of round 2's held-back failure.
- The report is candid: it names the reserve-backup risk and gives its own noisy full-game probes (+15 at s7453, -11 at s7454).
reviews.summary:
Verdict: revise. The realistic-reach idea is sound, but the backup that justifies each release is never made real, and the release ignores the opponent's card.

**The finding it changes rests on an unenforced reserve backup.** It changes only s7453, through pricing plus a reserve backup. Nothing makes that reserve land on home: deep-strike placement prefers forward objectives 10-15" from enemies. So 'home VP for one scoring' can become every remaining scoring, which the round-2-horizon rollout cannot see.

**In the bench the active part is the realistic reach.** It fires only for P1 in the Custodes mirror. On V9 it leans on the backup test after pass 2, which counts the Prosecutors; pass 3 then sends them to screen about 19" forward (V9 bench record /tmp/v9check/20261030_163105_CHK_M1_96021.record.json.gz). Each bench release therefore leaves obj_home_1 with nobody within a move for rounds 2-5.

**It ignores the opponent's card.** In 3 of the 7 pairings it unlocks (Meatgrinder, Outmanoeuvre, Punishment), the opponent is paid for holding our home.

**Merging onto 68c03f7 trades one problem for another.** The after-pass-3 test will likely veto every bench release, so the pairs come out identical. The pre-converted Normal move also skips 68c03f7's re-pricing and its hopeless-race (RACE-SKIP) check.

**Fixes:**
1. Pin the cheapest backup onto home in the same phase (on-board), or give a reserve backup a registered round-2 arrival on home. Otherwise price home at every remaining scoring.
2. Veto or price when the opponent's card pays per turn for our home.
3. Gate the destination with the same margin as the release.
4. Re-base on 68c03f7's after-pass-3 flow without pre-converting to a Normal move.

Before shipping, check the change over full games in the Custodes mirror (P1 seat). The designer's only full-game probe of the matching s7454-type release averaged -11 VP over 3 noisy seeds.

issues.situation: _keeper_release_check, the new destination rule (d) (patch lines ~109-135). The release is justified by `target`, which must not be a lost race and must score ≥ hold + KEEPER_RELEASE_MIN_GAIN (+ home_vp / sec_vp). The keeper is then sent to `best` instead: the fewest Normal-move turns among the keeper's candidates with score ≥ hold.score only, lost races allowed. `best` keeps the planner's score, turns_to_reach and race fields, which are Advance-pace values when the candidate was a long-trip Advance, while it executes a Normal move. FIX_FAR_TRIP is 0.0 at 5e70bc2, so nothing downstream rejects a lone lost race. Concrete case, Custodes-mirror fixture, P1's sole keeper U_CUSTODIAN_GUARD_F (M6) on obj_home_1: obj_center is 2 Normal turns; obj_nml_1 is 3 Normal turns (2 at Advance pace). If obj_nml_1 is the gate-passing target and the centre is a lost race whose halved score is still ≥ hold, the keeper walks into the centre. Under Determined Acquisition it then gives up home's priced 3 VP for a destination the AI itself values below hold + 3. The record, FAR-TRIP and OVERCOMMIT also read stale Advance-pace turns_to_reach and score for the walk.
issues.proposed_change: Choose (d)'s destination only among candidates that pass the same gate as `target`: not race_lost, arrives by round 5, and score ≥ hold + min_gain + home_vp/sec_vp. Evaluate each candidate after re-pricing it at Normal pace (turns = ceil(gap/M), contest race, distance penalty, reach horizon, reachability; e.g. V9R's _keeper_release_normal_pace). Use that re-priced dict as the target and record. If none qualifies, keep V9's target, or hold.

issues.situation: test_ai_fix_keeper_reach.gd does not pin what changes the finding, and is fragile on the merge target. (1) In every release board, the target obj_nml_1 is a 1-turn 'move' and is also the best-scoring candidate. So neither the soonest-objective pick nor the Advance→Normal conversion is exercised. That conversion is what turns s7453's base choice ('Advance obj_center', 2 Advance vs 3 Normal turns) into the measured Normal move. (2) test_priced_home_primary_releases_a_big_gain asserts release or hold depending on the scores it reads. A build that ignored home_vp would still pass; my arithmetic puts the Determined Acquisition gain at ≈12, so it lands in the release branch. (3) The report's base run ('7 passed, 3 failed' = 10 checks) does not match the 12-check file. With test 7 in the release branch, base should fail 4. (4) Only FIX_KEEPER_REACH is pinned. FIX_KEEPER_RELEASE has been 0.0 at HEAD since 14eb69f, so on the merge target _keeper_release_check is never called. The release checks then fail, and the shipped fix is inert unless the finalizer turns KEEPER-RELEASE back on.
issues.proposed_change: Pin FIX_KEEPER_RELEASE = 1.0 in _config_overrides and erase it at the end. Replace the conditional test with two deterministic boards: gain in [MIN_GAIN, MIN_GAIN + home_vp) asserting hold, and gain > MIN_GAIN + home_vp asserting release (control the gain by geometry or a KEEPER_RELEASE_MIN_GAIN override). Add a board where the best-scoring objective is a long Advance trip and a nearer objective beats holding: assert the nearer objective with action 'move' and Normal-pace turns. Add a board with an on-board backup and an enemy M6 at ~24" that releases (the bench path). Re-run on base with the final file and report exact counts.

issues.situation: Home VP is counted twice in the new margins. hold.score already contains home's VP: _evaluate_all_objectives does priority += vp_value * WEIGHT_VP_PER_POINT (1.2) for the held home, including primary per_objective/hold_min and secondary 'home'/'any' hints. _keeper_reach_home_vp / sec_vp then add the same VP again to the threshold. 'any' (Burden of Trust) is charged as a home-only cost although the destination pays it too. The release is therefore stricter than designed. Test 9's 'keeps' outcome may rest on this double count (with the 6-VP hint, hold.score rises by about 6.8 and the threshold by 6).
issues.proposed_change: Price only the part hold.score does not contain (e.g. the extra scorings lost while a reserve backup has not yet arrived), or drop home_vp/sec_vp from the threshold. Do not treat 'any' hints as a cost of leaving home.

issues.situation: Realistic reach model in _keeper_reach_threat. The walk is labelled 'Move + 12" (a Normal move and an Advance)', but the engine's Advance is a D6 (≤6", MovementPhase._resolve_advance_roll), so the walk is 6" more cautious than its stated model. That is harmless, but it is what keeps the asymmetric fixture's Custodes keeper home (Wazdakka M14 ~24.3" vs 26"). The charge path adds +6" only when effect_advance_and_charge is already set. An Ork army with an unused Waaagh! can Advance and charge next turn, so it is under-reached by 6" against our units near home (the LESSONS failure mode). The charge distance is also centre to centre, ignoring base radii.
issues.proposed_change: Document the walk as M + 6 Advance + 6 slack (or tighten it deliberately). In the charge path, add +6" when the enemy has an unused army-wide advance-and-charge rule, and measure base edge to base edge.

issues.situation: The reserve backup guarantee is weak. Any reserve unit of ours counts, but Strategic Reserves must be set up wholly within 6" of a battlefield edge, so they may not reach a central home on arrival. The reserve-arrival AI is not steered to the empty home. The post-pass-2 'backup sent elsewhere' test passes automatically for reserves: assignments has no entry, so b_oid defaults to home. Home can then stay empty in rounds 2-5, which is the report's own main full-game risk.
issues.proposed_change: Count only reserves that can be set up in range of home on arrival (Deep Strike, or Strategic Reserves when home's range is within 6" of an edge). Flag the released home so the round-2 reserve-arrival planner prefers it.

issues.situation: Merge onto V9R (68c03f7, keeper_release_rev_vs_v9.patch), which deletes the post-pass-2 release block and applies releases after pass 3. This patch's '[KEEPER_REACH] ... released' report loop sits right after the deleted block. After the merge it runs before any release and never prints, and the report's firing counts rely on that line. (d) pre-sets action 'move', so V9R's `kr_first and action == "advance"` path (_keeper_release_normal_pace, TOO-LATE, RACE-SKIP) never runs for KEEPER-REACH releases. The return contract is compatible (`kr.has("target")`).
issues.proposed_change: When finalizing on V9R, move the report loop after the post-pass-3 release block, and send (d)'s Normal-move conversion through _keeper_release_normal_pace and its gates instead of pre-setting 'move'.

issues.situation: Narration and report accuracy. The player-facing coordination_note for a KEEPER-REACH release reuses V9's sentence, 'our primary does not pay for it ... can re-take it in one move'. That is false under Determined Acquisition and false for a reserve backup, and test 1 asserts on that sentence. The report says the trigger needs 'our reserves non-empty', but the reach relaxation fires with on-board backups and no reserves; that is exactly the Custodes-mirror P1 bench case. The report also names hold_more as s7433's blocker, but condemned_left is hit first (same outcome).
issues.proposed_change: Build kr.why from `reach` when it is non-empty (priced VP, reserve unit, realistic reach). Correct the trigger description and add an explicit bench-firing estimate to the report.

reviews.fires_in_bench:
Rare, and only in the Custodes mirror. Estimated from trigger conditions and fixture geometry; I could not run it (instructed not to run Godot).

**Shared facts:** none of the three fixtures has any unit in reserves. So the reserve-backup part (b) and the enemy Strategic Reserves relaxation never fire, and those are what change s7453. Only two parts can fire: the realistic-reach re-check, and the priced primary with an on-board backup. Both apply in round 1 only.

**Custodes mirror** (first_turn_player 1):
- Only P1 can fire. U_CUSTODIAN_GUARD_F is the sole unit on obj_home_1 and is not fragile.
- On-board backups exist: Guard C 0.7", Prosecutors 0.8", Guard D 4.3".
- The nearest enemy is 23.4" from the home area. That is inside V9's 24" block but outside the realistic 18" walk and the 19" charge (nearest charge pair is 26.5").
- P1's card must be one of 9/25 pairings (bench dispositions cycle by seed): 7 already pass V9's primary check, plus Determined Acquisition (+3 VP) and Secure Asset (+4 VP). The other 16 have unpriceable rules and keep the keeper.
- No Defend Stronghold or Burden of Trust may be drawn (about 80%).
- The trip must beat holding by ≥5 (+3/+4). My rough score arithmetic for Guard F (the centre is likely a lost race; obj_nml_1 is a 2-turn Advance trip) suggests this often fails.
- Expect about 0–25% of games where the candidate plays P1 (upper bound ≈29%), i.e. at most a handful of ~42 pairs.
- P2 essentially never: P1's first move brings models inside 18–19".

**Orks mirror:** ~0. Four units start on each home, and the M12 Orks at 23.4" are inside the realistic 24" walk.

**Custodes vs Orks:** ~0. Wazdakka (M14, ~24.3") is inside the 26" walk of the Custodes home. Five Ork units sit on the Ork home, and the Custodes move first.

**Precondition:** with FIX_KEEPER_RELEASE at 0.0 (HEAD since 14eb69f), it fires nowhere.
reviews.strengths:
- **Param gating:** every new path is gated by FIX_KEEPER_REACH and battle_round ≤ KEEPER_REACH_MAX_ROUND. With 0, or from round 2, behaviour is identical to 5e70bc2. The only trace is an extra empty 'reach' key and a report loop gated on it.
- **V9 releases untouched:** when V9 would release, `reach` stays empty and nothing changes (s7437 kept).
- **Rules-correct reserves:** the 11e assumptions match the engine. Strategic Reserves cannot be set up in the opponent's zone before round 3 (MovementPhase 20.04 check); Deep Strike can.
- **Conservative where it should be:** fragile keepers, PM-3 hold earmarks, require_hold_home, and the 16/25 cards with marker/hold_more mechanics all still keep the keeper.
- **Principled on s7454:** it keeps the keeper there because of a rule-legal round-2 Deep Strike onto an empty home, not because of the max-roll reach.
- **Report claims hold up:** I checked them against the saves. s7453: P2 moves first so enemy_round=1, Determined Acquisition home_vp 3, Allarus/Guard D as reserve backup, centre and obj_nml_2 tie at 3 Normal turns so score decides. s7454: P2 first so enemy_round=2, P2's Allarus is deep_strike. s7455/s7438/s7406 keepers are fragile. s7420 and s7433 cards cannot be priced.
- **Cost and logging:** cheap (once per sole home keeper per plan, no hot loop). Every new decision is logged with [KEEPER_REACH]; no existing log removed.
- **Tests:** they drive the real _evaluate_all_objectives / _assign_units_to_objectives path and pin the realistic walk boundary, the charge-then-consolidate path, the reserve backup, the Strategic Reserves relaxation, Deep Strike reserves, require_hold_home and param 0.
- **Measurable:** unlike V9, it can plausibly fire in the Custodes-mirror bench.
reviews.summary:
**Verdict: revise.** The idea is sound, but two major issues need fixing first.

FIX_KEEPER_REACH widens V9's KEEPER-RELEASE in round 1 with three relaxations, plus a destination rule:
- A realistic reach replaces the max-roll threat check.
- A reserve unit counts as the backup when no unit can step onto home.
- A primary card that pays for home is priced instead of vetoed.
- **Rule (d):** the released keeper makes a Normal move to the objective it reaches soonest.

Param 0 restores the base exactly. It changes s7453 to the measured Normal move to obj_center and keeps s7454 on purpose; the report's checks agree with the code and the saves.

**Major issues:**
1. **Rule (d) is decoupled from the release gate.** The release must clear hold + 5 (+ priced home VP) on a target that is not a lost race. The destination only needs score ≥ hold, may be a lost race, and keeps Advance-pace scores and turns for a Normal walk. FAR-TRIP is off at 5e70bc2, so nothing downstream catches it.
2. **The tests do not pin the fix.** No test exercises (d)'s soonest pick or its Advance→Normal conversion, which is what makes s7453 match. The priced-primary test is adaptive. The base-failure count (10 checks) does not match the 12-check file. FIX_KEEPER_RELEASE is not pinned, and it has been 0.0 at HEAD since 14eb69f, so the fix is inert there and its release checks fail.

**Minor issues:**
- Home VP and secondary-card VP are counted twice in the new margins.
- The walk is mislabelled (Advance is a D6); the charge path ignores an unused Waaagh!.
- Any reserve unit counts as a backup, with no guarantee it can arrive on home.
- Merge hazards with V9R: the report loop goes dead, and the pre-set Normal move bypasses its re-pricing.
- The player-facing narration is false for these releases, and the report's trigger summary is wrong.

**Bench:** the part that changes s7453 (reserve backup) cannot occur in any of the three fixtures. Only a minority of P1 games in the Custodes mirror can fire, through the realistic-reach and priced-primary parts.

scores.note: Only design that changes a finding to the measured alternative. At s7453 it orders U_CUSTODIAN_GUARD_B_P2 to make a Normal move to obj_center (+6.17 [3.42, 8.91] n36), with the right unit, objective and mode. I checked this against the s7453 save and the code. P2 moves first, so V9's threat test is clear. V9 is blocked only by the card (Determined Acquisition counts home) and by having no on-board backup. The design prices home at 3 VP, counts P2's Deep Strike reserves (Allarus, Guard D) as the backup, and rule (d) picks obj_center (3 Normal turns, tied with obj_nml_2, higher score) over V9's target obj_nml_1 (4 turns). s7437 is kept and no guardrail moves. Weaknesses: (1) s7454 is held on purpose because of the Deep Strike reserve, although the 36-seed horizon covered that round-2 window and still favoured leaving; the only counter-evidence is a 3-seed noisy probe. (2) It reaches s7453 for a wrong reason: branch B never left home. (3) The reserve backup is unenforced, the opponent's card is ignored, and (d) is not gated like the release. (4) The priced test is adaptive, (d) is untested, FIX_KEEPER_RELEASE is not pinned, and the base count (7+3) does not match the 12 checks. (5) Bench: on V9 about 4% of games, and those releases leave home with nobody near. On V9R the finished-plan backup check vetoes them (about 0 fires). At HEAD it is inert (FIX_KEEPER_RELEASE = 0.0).

Best diagnosis of s7453, which I confirmed on the save. area-large-21 spans y 1720-2000 and the keeper stands on its far edge (2 of 3 bases in range). An 8-inch move toward the centre crosses the ruin and keeps all 3 (OC 6 -> 9), so branch B kept home. But the build skips lost races (obj_center is one at s7453) and ranks trips by capture score. So at s7453 it creeps toward obj_nml_1 instead, and the designer's own 6 seeds show no gain (E(hold-fix) +0.67 [-3.96, 5.30]). s7454 is unchanged, and the neutral guardrail s7433 becomes an unmeasured creep toward obj_nml_2. It fails the evidence gate. Safety: need = enemy OC + 1 allows a permanent cut of home OC, and it applies to any objective in any round with no margin. The 'move' relabel lands before pass 2.5, and in the bench fixture Custodian Guard are melee seekers (spear ranged S4 A2), so a keeper can be sent hunting with no backfill. The ROLLOUT override keeps the keeper_reach_* keys. Bench: 0 round-1 fires. In the V9 record (seed 96021) P1 Guard F's only non-lost trip above hold is obj_center (27.95 vs 22.91), and a 6-inch move toward it takes all 5 bases off area-large-14. P2's trips are all lost races, and the Ork homes start with 4-5 units.

verdict.reasons:
Totals are the sum of the five 0-10 scores. Game wins because it is the only design that meets the gates. Its decision check moves a measured finding to the measured alternative with the right unit, objective and mode: at s7453 it makes a Normal move to obj_center. No guardrail moves, and its core reach test fails on base.

Root fails the evidence gate. It skips lost races and ranks trips by capture score, so at s7453 it never tries obj_center (a lost race there) and creeps toward obj_nml_1. The designer's own 6 seeds measured no gain for that move. It also leaves s7454 unchanged and changes the neutral guardrail s7433 to an unmeasured move.

Root's diagnosis is still the right explanation of s7453. On the save, the keeper stands on the far edge of the 7-inch-deep home ruin (area-large-21), and the measured centre move crosses the ruin and keeps all 3 bases in range (OC 6 -> 9). Game reaches the same physical move for a wrong reason: it believes it gives home up, prices that at 3 VP and leans on an unenforced reserve backup. Its required changes therefore graft root's keeps-home check, so that s7453 is released at no home cost. Elsewhere the home cost must be real.

Neither design can show anything in the bench on the merge base (V9R). I checked the V9 bench record /tmp/v9check/20261030_163105_CHK_M1_96021.record.json.gz against the fixture mirror_custodes_2000_postdeploy:
- Root cannot fire in round 1.
- Game fires only for P1 in the Custodes mirror, and only on V9. There the post-pass-2 backup test counts the unassigned Prosecutors, whom pass 3 then sends to screen at (760,1446), about 20 inches past home. V9R's finished-plan check vetoes that release.

Game is safe enough to finalize after the required changes. It acts in round 1 only, on our home keeper only, and FIX_KEEPER_REACH=0 or battle round >= 2 restores base exactly. It also moves a durable unit forward, which is the opposite of round 2's held-back failure.

It is unlikely to pass the bench ship rule as written. Run the firing census first.

Narrow was dropped by its designer. Its v2 fixed s7454 only by ignoring a rule-legal round-2 Deep Strike, and broke a V9 test.

My decode and geometry scratch files are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-warhammer-40k-godot/72451711-ff9e-5f4b-a27c-d739a3534701/scratchpad/judge/.
required_changes:
Rebase on V9R (68c03f7).
- Delete the post-pass-2 '[KEEPER_REACH] ... released' loop.
- Make every new early exit in _keeper_release_check return {"kept": why}.
- Let V9R's post-pass-3 block apply KEEPER-REACH releases, with its still-hold check, finished-plan backup check and melee chase gate, and print the [KEEPER_REACH] release line there.
- KEEPER-REACH runs only inside _keeper_release_check, so ship it only together with FIX_KEEPER_RELEASE = 1. HEAD has 0.0 since 14eb69f, and at that value this patch is inert.

Destination rule (d).
- Stop setting action 'move' on the planner's Advance-pace candidate.
- For each candidate that passes the planner-score floor below, build the Normal-move version with _keeper_release_normal_pace. Drop it if too_late or race_hopeless (RACE-SKIP) rejects that version.
- Require the planner score >= hold.score + the home VP this release gives up (0 on the keeps-home path below).
- Take the fewest Normal turns (ties: score, then distance). Act on and record the re-priced dict (push_front into _last_movement_candidates, as V9R does).
- Do NOT add a 'not race_lost' or 'hold + MIN_GAIN' gate on the destination: the measured s7453 move (obj_center, 20.8) is a lost race.

Make the home cost real.
(a) Port root's _keeper_reach_oc_in_range. Predict the keeper's Normal move to the chosen destination with _compute_movement_toward_target. If the keeper keeps at least the OC it has in range now on home's hosting area (no OC lost), release with no home VP and no backup. At s7453: area-large-21, OC 6 -> 9. Add root's executor re-check: REMAIN_STATIONARY when the executed destinations keep less.
(b) Otherwise:
- A reserve unit counts as the backup only if it can be set up within range of home when it arrives (Deep Strike, or Strategic Reserves whose legal set-up band reaches home's range).
- When the backup is a reserve unit, price a card that pays for home at every remaining scoring (rounds 2-5), not at one.

Read the opponent's primary in the KEEPER-REACH branch: MissionManager.player_primary_missions[str(3 - player)].
- Keep the keeper when that card has a hold_enemy_home rule scoring at eot or command in rounds >= 2 (Meatgrinder 5 VP eot, Outmanoeuvre 10 VP eot in PrimaryMissionData11e).
- Add an end-of-game hold_enemy_home rule's VP (Punishment 8, others 5-10) to the release margin once.

In _keeper_reach_threat's charge path:
- Measure base edge to base edge (subtract both base radii) instead of model centre to centre.
- Add 6 inches when the enemy army still has an army-wide advance-and-charge ability it can use next turn (an unused Waaagh!), not only when flags.effect_advance_and_charge is already set.
- Correct the walk comment: Move + D6 Advance + 6-inch margin.

Tests (test_ai_fix_keeper_reach.gd):
- Pin FIX_KEEPER_RELEASE = 1.0 and erase it at the end.

High.
1. The design only runs inside _keeper_release_check. At HEAD FIX_KEEPER_RELEASE is 0.0 (since 14eb69f), so the patch is inert unless it ships together with V9R's KEEPER-RELEASE.
2. It conflicts with 68c03f7. That commit deletes the post-pass-2 block the report loop is anchored after, changes _keeper_release_check's returns to {kept: why}, and re-prices the walk only for 'advance' targets. The patch's pre-set 'move' skips V9R's normal-pace re-pricing and its TOO-LATE and RACE-SKIP checks.

4. Where it does fire (real games with Deep Strike reserves and cards that pay for home), its main costs lie beyond the one-round rollout horizon: an empty home in rounds 2-5, reserves not steered back to home, and opponent hold_enemy_home cards. Required changes 3 and 4 cover these.
